smbd_deltas: confirmed per mariowiki: smbd replaces the nes warp-zone room's 3-pipe world-select with a room containing brick blocks, three ? blocks, 22 coins, and a power-up brick block - i.e. smbd 1-2 likely has no functional warp zone / world skip in this spot, or it is relocated elsewhere (not found in sources used). the warp_zone area entry and warps[] array above describe the measured NES layout; do not assume they apply unmodified to smbd until the gbc map is pixel-measured the same way. total coin count also differs: 68 coins (nes) vs 90 coins (smbd challenge mode) per mariowiki, implying additional coins were added somewhere in the smbd layout beyond just the warp-zone-room replacement.
confidence_notes: this level's skeleton is no longer prose-derived: the floor pits, ceiling runs (including the two ceiling_gap spans), the three piranha pipe columns, the warp zone's pipe order/columns/world numbers, the closing staircase's shape, the flagpole's clearance and the castle's offset were extracted programmatically from the official nes 1-2 map image (3072x720, stacked as a 192-column underground band plus two above-ground band-0 segments) by classifying 16x16 cells against a tile sheet cut from the same image, cross-checked pixel by pixel where the ascii/grid extraction was ambiguous. those items carry "confidence": "measured". individual coin/block/enemy placement inside the underground run remains "approx" - the extraction is reliable on the skeleton and rough on small objects (documented in the spec this was built from), so counts and rough positions are kept, exact cells are not claimed as measured. two findings from this pass, previously flagged as things to investigate rather than paper over: (1) the real level is three physical areas - an above-ground start (castle, flat ground, the entry pipe), the underground main run, and an above-ground ending (piranha pipe, staircase, flagpole, castle) - but this engine compiles one typed grid per level plus pipe-triggered sub-areas that return to where they were entered; it cannot express "overworld, then underground, then overworld again" within one level. the above-ground start is therefore not rendered at all (matches the pre-existing entry_pipe_x() skip), and the above-ground ending is appended as more columns of the same underground-typed grid rather than switching visual type, so it renders correctly playable but with the cave ceiling still overhead - a real fidelity gap. the measured relative geometry of the ending (stair shape, the 9-column flag clearance, the 4-column castle offset) is preserved exactly; only its absolute column is re-anchored past the underground run's own last column (191) because the grid has nowhere else to put it. the smallest fix is not a full multi-segment engine, it is letting a level bible declare per-column-range palette/ceiling overrides so a tail of an underground-typed grid can look and read as sky - i.e. keep one grid, stop tying its look to a single global type. this pass adds the smaller, unconditionally useful half of that idea now: a new terrain kind, ceiling_gap, that lets an underground level's roof have real holes (used here for the entry shaft and the lift shaft) instead of the unconditional full-width roof apply_ceiling() used to stamp. (2) the three warp-zone pipes lead to worlds 2, 3 and 4, which this rom does not have (kLevelCount is 4, world one only). compile_level.py used to clamp an unresolvable warp target to the last level of world one, which meant pressing down on the "world 4" pipe silently sent the player into 1-4 - a real bug, not a hypothetical one, verified by reading main.c's kStatePipeDown handling. this pass replaces the clamp with WARP_UNBUILT (0xFF): the pipe is still built, in the correct order, still carrying its real destination in this file, but flow_warp_under_player()'s existing 0xFF-is-nothing convention (already used for every other pipe check in main.c) makes pressing down over it a no-op instead of a jump. no engine (.c) change was needed for this half; the fix lives entirely in compile_level.py. verified in the host tests that entering each of the three pipes neither crashes nor changes level_number.
